title: Operating Systems (Tanenbaum)
blurb: Processes, memory, files, I/O, deadlocks, virtualization, multiprocessors and security, with runnable simulations of every classic algorithm and two real-system case studies.
sources: Tanenbaum & Bos, Modern Operating Systems, 4th ed., ch. 1–12

modules.title: 1 · Introduction
modules.summary: What an operating system is, the hardware it tames, and the concepts and system calls it offers.

lessons.title: What an operating system is, its history and its many forms
Hardware review: CPUs, memory, devices and booting
Core concepts, system calls and kernel structure

modules.title: 2 · Processes and Threads
modules.summary: The process model, threads, races and mutual exclusion, semaphores to monitors, and CPU scheduling.

lessons.title: Processes and threads
Race conditions and mutual exclusion
Semaphores, monitors, message passing and the classic problems
CPU scheduling

modules.title: 3 · Memory Management
modules.summary: Address spaces, swapping, paging, TLBs, page replacement and segmentation.

lessons.title: Address spaces, swapping and free-space management
Virtual memory: paging, page tables and TLBs
Page replacement algorithms
Paging design, implementation issues and segmentation

modules.title: 4 · File Systems
modules.summary: Files and directories, on-disk layout, journaling, the VFS, and how file systems are kept fast and consistent.

lessons.title: Files and directories
File-system implementation
Management, optimisation and example file systems

modules.title: 5 · Input/Output
modules.summary: Device hardware, the layered I/O software stack, disks and RAID, clocks, terminals and power.

lessons.title: I/O hardware and the layers of I/O software
Disks, RAID and disk-arm scheduling
Clocks, user interfaces and power management

modules.title: 6 · Deadlocks
modules.summary: When processes wait for each other forever: modelling, detection, recovery, avoidance and prevention.

lessons.title: Deadlock: conditions, modelling, detection and recovery
Deadlock avoidance, the banker's algorithm and prevention

modules.title: 7 · Virtualization and the Cloud
modules.summary: Hypervisors, how privileged instructions, memory and devices are virtualised, containers and clouds.

lessons.title: Hypervisors and CPU virtualization techniques
Memory and I/O virtualization, containers and clouds

modules.title: 8 · Multiple Processor Systems
modules.summary: Shared-memory multiprocessors, message-passing multicomputers and distributed systems.

lessons.title: Multiprocessors: hardware, synchronisation and scheduling
Multicomputers and distributed systems

modules.title: 9 · Security
modules.summary: Threats, access control, formal models, cryptography, authentication, and how attacks and defences work conceptually.

lessons.title: Threat models, access control and formal models
Cryptography basics and authentication
Classes of attack and the defences against them

modules.title: 10 · Case Study: Linux
modules.summary: How Linux (and Android on top of it) realises processes, scheduling, memory, I/O, files and security.

lessons.title: Linux: history, structure, processes and scheduling
Linux: memory, I/O, file systems, security and Android

modules.title: 11 · Case Study: Windows
modules.summary: The NT architecture: executive, objects and handles, threads, memory manager, I/O stack, NTFS and security.

lessons.title: Windows: structure, objects, processes and threads
Windows: memory, caching, I/O, NTFS and security

modules.title: 12 · Operating System Design
modules.summary: Designing interfaces, choosing structures, tuning performance and managing the project — then the interview round-up.

lessons.title: Design goals, interfaces and implementation
Performance, project management and trends
OS interview essentials
